16.11 Way one, verification

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route vrf RED ipv6 2001:db8:c:206::/64 detail
      SRv6 Headend: H.Encaps.Red [f3216], SID-list {fcbb:bb01:6:e004::}

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route ipv6 fcbb:bb01:6::/48
  Known via "isis CORE", distance 115, metric 3001, SRv6-locator (algo 128), type level-2
    fe80::5454:ff:fec1:58eb, from 2001:db8:100::6, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1, Protected

Captured, ping6 from CE-A to CE-B in RED:
  PE1 to P3   fcbb:bb01:6:e004::   hop limit 255
  P3 to P5    fcbb:bb01:6:e004::   hop limit 254
  P5 to PE6   fcbb:bb01:6:e004::   hop limit 253
  • Method 1 uses the tested FA128 service allocation.
  • RED IPv6 uses the SID of PE6 from the FA128 block, fcbb:bb01.
  • IS-IS routes that locator in algorithm 128, with metric 3001, through P3. It has TI-LFA protection in the same algorithm.
  • On the wire, the destination does not change. No router removes a micro-SID. Each router only routes fcbb:bb01:6 in algorithm 128. This is the simplest method.

16.12 A trap: up, but not on Algo 128

segment-list PE6-ALGO128
 srv6
  index 10 sid fcbb:bb01:6::
policy GREEN-C400
 color 400 end-point ipv6 2001:db8:100::6

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show cef vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
    SRv6 H.Encaps.Red SID-list {fcbb:bb00:6:e008::}
    0     Y   GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1    fe80::5454:ff:fec1:58eb

Captured: PE1 to P3, then P4 to PE6. Nothing on P3 to P5 or P5 to PE6.
  • One more case. Can we write an explicit policy with one segment, the algorithm 128 node SID of PE6?
  • The color is 400, with one segment: fcbb:bb01:6::. The policy came up.
  • But look at CEF. It shows only the service SID, from the usual block. PE1 does not install the final node SID, as Episode 15 showed. Thus the packet has no information about algorithm 128.
  • The packet went to P3. Then it followed algorithm 0 and arrived at PE6 from P4. The policy was up, but the path was not the path in its name. We removed it.

Ep17 · A Method, and SRv6 OAM

17.1 Layer 1: local, on the egress

Router / tool: PE6

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show segment-routing srv6 locator
Name                  ID       Algo  Prefix                    Status   Flags
FA128                 1        128   fcbb:bb01:6::/48          Up       U
MAIN                  2        0     fcbb:bb00:6::/48          Up       U

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show segment-routing srv6 manager
    Block fcbb:bb01::/32:
        Number of SIDs free: 7675
        Max SIDs: 7680
        Status: Resource Available
  • Layer 1, on PE6. PE6 owns the SIDs.
  • The two locators are up: MAIN in algorithm 0 and FA128 in algorithm 128. The healthy sign is the status Up.
  • The manager shows the SID resources for each block, and many are free. Episode 19 uses these numbers again. If a locator is down or a block is full, stop here. The higher layers cannot operate.

17.2 Layer 2: the IGP

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show isis segment-routing srv6 locators
Name                  ID       Algo  Prefix                    Status
FA128                 1        128   fcbb:bb01:6::/48          Active
MAIN                  2        0     fcbb:bb00:6::/48          Active

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route ipv6 fcbb:bb00:6::/48
  Known via "isis CORE", distance 115, metric 31, SRv6-locator, type level-2
    fe80::5454:ff:fe66:75e1, from 2001:db8:100::6, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0, Protected
    fe80::5454:ff:fec1:58eb, from 2001:db8:100::6, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1, Backup (TI-LFA)
      Repair Node(s): 2001:db8:100::5
  • Layer 2 is the IGP. We examine it on the two ends.
  • On PE6, IS-IS shows the two locators as active. Fault A in Episode 3 failed at this point. The locator was up locally, but IS-IS did not advertise it.
  • On PE1, the locator is a route from IS-IS, with metric 31.
  • The primary path shows protected, and there is a TI-LFA backup through repair node P5. The healthy sign is the route on the ingress.
  • A loopback ping does not replace this check. In Episode 3, the loopback ping was correct, but the service did not operate.

17.3 Layer 3: forwarding

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show cef ipv6 fcbb:bb00:6::/48
fcbb:bb00:6::/48, version 130, SRv6 Headend
   via fe80::5454:ff:fe66:75e1/128, GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0, 8 dependencies, protected
   via fe80::5454:ff:fec1:58eb/128, GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1, 13 dependencies, backup (TI-LFA)
    next hop fe80::5454:ff:fec1:58eb/128, Repair Node(s): 2001:db8:100::5
    SRv6 H.Insert.Red SID-list {fcbb:bb00:3:e005::}

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show cef ipv6 fcbb:bb00:6:e004::/64
fcbb:bb00:6:e004::/64, version 136, SRv6 Endpoint uDT4
    next hop VRF - 'BLUE', table - 0xe0000002
    0     Y   recursive                 Lookup in table
  • Layer 3 is forwarding. The RIB shows what the router wants to do. CEF shows what it does.
  • On PE1, the primary path goes through P2. The dependencies are the service routes that resolve through it.
  • The backup is also installed, with its repair segment, as in Episode 9.
  • On PE6, the entry for the service SID is a lookup in BLUE. The healthy signs are an interface on the ingress and the correct VRF on the egress. In Episode 3, the forwarding table showed unresolved and drop.

17.4 Layer 4: the service

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show bgp vpnv4 unicast vrf BLUE 10.1.6.0/24 detail
    2001:db8:100::6 C:100 (bsid: fcbb:bb00:1:e008::) (metric 30) from 2001:db8:100::6
      Received Label 0xe0040
      Extended community: Color:100 RT:65000:100
      SR policy color 100, up, not-registered, bsid fcbb:bb00:1:e008::
       SID Locator: fcbb:bb00:6::/48, RIB metric: 31
        T:1(Sid information), Sid:fcbb:bb00:6::(Transposed), Behavior:63
  • Layer 4 is the service. One command shows most of it. This is BLUE from Episode 15.
  • This is the SID, with its label and behavior. If it is incorrect or not there, the egress did not allocate it. This was fault B in Episode 3.
  • These are the color and the route target. With an incorrect route target, the VRF imports nothing, as in Episode 12.
  • If the route has a color, look at the policy. Remember Episodes 15 and 16: a policy can be up, but it can do something that you did not want.
  • This is the locator check, metric 31. If it shows inaccessible, go back to layer 2.

17.5 Layer 5: end to end

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf BLUE 10.1.6.2 source 10.1.1.1 count 3
!!!
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/3 ms

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#traceroute vrf BLUE 10.1.6.2 source 10.1.1.1 probe 1 timeout 1 maxttl 5
 1  10.46.0.1 3 msec
 2  10.1.6.2 2 msec
  • Layer 5 is end to end.
  • We send a ping in the VRF, from the BLUE address of PE1 to CE-B. It gets a reply.
  • Then a VRF traceroute shows PE6, then CE-B. As Episode 13 showed, the core is not visible in the VRF.
  • A small ping that goes through shows only that small packets go through in one direction. In Episodes 7 and 14, only large packets showed the faults. Test with different sizes. If you are not sure, capture.

17.6 OAM: pinging SIDs

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping fcbb:bb00:6:: source 2001:db8:100::1 count 3
!!!
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/3 ms
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping fcbb:bb00:6:e000:: source 2001:db8:100::1 count 3
!!!
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/3 ms
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping fcbb:bb00:6:e004:: source 2001:db8:100::1 count 3 timeout 1
!!!
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/4/5 ms
  • Now the operations tools. First, can you send a ping to a SID?
  • The node SID of PE6 gets a reply.
  • One of the adjacency SIDs of PE6 gets a reply.
  • The BLUE service SID, a uDT4, also gets a reply.

17.7 OAM: traceroute

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#traceroute ipv6 fcbb:bb00:6:: source 2001:db8:100::1 probe 1 timeout 1 maxttl 6
Tracing the route to fcbb:bb00:6::
 1  2001:db8:200:12::1 3 msec
 2  2001:db8:200:24::1 2 msec
 3  2001:db8:100::6 2 msec

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#traceroute ipv6 fcbb:bb00:6:: source 2001:db8:100::1 probe 1 timeout 1 maxttl 6 srv6
% Invalid input detected at '^' marker.
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#traceroute ipv6 fcbb:bb00:6:: srv6
% Invalid input detected at '^' marker.

! In the help tree of this release (not run):
traceroute segment-routing srv6 policy name <name>
  • Now traceroute. We make four points.
  • Point 1: a plain traceroute works. To the node SID of PE6, it shows P2, P4, then PE6, on the IGP path.
  • Point 2: Cisco documents two SRv6 forms of traceroute. Neither is in the ipv6 help tree of XRd 26.2.2. Our statement is only about the ipv6 syntax.
  • Point 3: this release has traceroute segment-routing srv6 policy name, followed by the name. It traces a policy. We did not run it.
  • Point 4: a document does not always match your release. Use the question mark on your router, and test the syntax.

17.8 Traceroute into a container

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#traceroute fcbb:bb00:3:5:6:: source 2001:db8:100::1
 1  2001:db8:200:12::1 3 msec 1 msec 1 msec
 2  2001:db8:100::3 1 msec 1 msec 1 msec
 3  2001:db8:200:23:: 1 msec 1 msec 1 msec
 4  2001:db8:200:24::1 2 msec 1 msec 1 msec
 5  2001:db8:100::5 2 msec 4 msec 1 msec
 6  2001:db8:200:45:: 1 msec 1 msec 1 msec
 7   *  *  *
 8   *  *  *
  • Now a traceroute to an address that we made manually: fcbb:bb00:3:5:6::. This is the loose path of Episode 15.
  • Hop 1 is P2.
  • Hop 2 is P3. It replies from its loopback, because the address was its node SID. Then hop 3 is P2 again. This is the first U-turn of Episode 15, and we see it without a capture.
  • Then P4, then P5 from its loopback, then P4 again. This is the second U-turn.
  • PE6 does not reply. This agrees with Episodes 4 and 5. The checksum of the probe uses the first destination, thus the last node discards it. We see the path, but not the last hop.

Ep18 · Four Faults, Live

18.1 Fault 1: capture the path

Router / tool: CE-A and tshark

CE-A:~$ sudo ping -c 2 -s 1300 172.16.30.6
2 packets transmitted, 2 packets received, 0% packet loss
CE-A:~$ sudo ping -c 2 -s 1400 172.16.30.6          (no reply)

$ tshark -r <capture file> -Y "ipv6.nxt == 143 or icmpv6.type == 2" -T fields -e frame.len -e ipv6.src -e ipv6.dst
# PE1 to P2
1396   2001:db8:100::1   fcbb:bb00:6:e007::    1300-byte ping, request
1396   2001:db8:100::6   fcbb:bb00:1:e00b::    1300-byte ping, reply
1496   2001:db8:100::1   fcbb:bb00:6:e007::    1400-byte ping, request
1294   2001:db8:100::1   (to PE1's loopback)   Packet Too Big, MTU 1336
# P2 to P4, and P4 to PE6
1396   the 1300-byte request and reply only
  • Layer 5 tells us where to look: the wire. We captured on three core links while CE-A sent pings of three sizes. We read each file with tshark.
  • The 1300-byte pings are answered. The 1400-byte pings get no reply.
  • The 1300-byte pings are 1396-byte frames, and they cross the core in both directions.
  • The 1400-byte request leaves PE1 as a 1496-byte frame, and it arrives at P2.
  • P2 sent an ICMPv6 Packet Too Big to the encapsulation source, the loopback of PE1. For a Layer 2 frame, PE1 cannot use this message. Thus the customer gets no message.
  • On the links from P2 to P4 and from P4 to PE6, there are only the small frames. The large frames stop at P2. Thus the fault is on P2, on its link to P4.

18.2 Fault 1: the cause

Router / tool: P2

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:P2#show ipv6 interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1
  MTU is 1514 (1400 is available to IPv6)

Packet Too Big, captured on PE1 to P2:
    Type: Packet Too Big (2)
    MTU: 1336
        Source Address: 2001:db8:100::1
        Destination Address: fcbb:bb00:6:e007::

Fix on P2:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1
 no ipv6 mtu
  • Layer 3 on P2 shows the cause.
  • The interface MTU is still 1514, but IPv6 can use only 1400. Somebody set an IPv6 MTU on this one link. This is the fault. In a real network, it is often a change on one link that nobody relates to a customer.
  • The Packet Too Big contains the outer packet from PE1, to the Layer 2 SID of PE6. Its MTU field shows 1336, not 1400.
  • We tested this later on XRd and on XRv9000. Both platforms show the MTU minus 64 when the destination route has a TI-LFA repair path. With no repair path, the value is correct.
  • Forwarding always uses the real MTU. We think that the 64 bytes are space for a repair header, but Cisco does not document this. Trust the capture, not only the reported value.
  • We removed one line, and the 1418-byte ping went through again. The finding: test with different sizes. When a size fails, capture on each link until the packet disappears.

18.3 Fault 1: the configuration change

Router / tool: P2

! On P2, toward P4
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1
 ipv6 mtu 1400

# Largest customer IP packet over E-Line with this limit:
# 1400 - 40 (outer IPv6 header) - 14 (inner Ethernet header) = 1346 bytes
  • This is the change on P2.
  • One command sets the IPv6 MTU to 1400 on the link toward P4. The interface MTU stays at 1514.
  • The arithmetic: 1400, minus 40 for the outer IPv6 header, minus 14 for the inner Ethernet header, is 1346. A customer packet larger than 1346 bytes cannot cross this link. This agrees with the pings: 1300 passed and 1400 failed.

18.4 Fault 2: one direction

Router / tool: CE-A and tshark

CE-A:~$ sudo ping -c 3 -W 2 -I 10.1.1.2 10.1.6.2
3 packets transmitted, 0 packets received, 100% packet loss

$ tshark -r <capture file> -Y "icmp.type == 8 or icmp.type == 0" -T fields -e ipv6.dst -e icmp.type | sort | uniq -c
# CE-A to PE1       3 requests
# PE1 to P2         3 requests   fcbb:bb00:3:5:6:e004::
# P4 to PE6         3 requests   fcbb:bb00:6:e004::
# PE6 to CE-B       3 requests, and 3 replies from CE-B
  • Fault 2. BLUE does not operate: CE-A cannot ping CE-B. On PE1, all the layers look correct for the prefix of CE-B. Thus we go directly to the wire.
  • Three requests leave CE-A, and no replies come back.
  • The requests go through the core to the BLUE service SID on PE6.
  • CE-B receives them and replies three times. The replies arrive at PE6 and stop there. The forward direction is correct. The return direction is broken. A ping cannot show which direction is broken. A capture can.

18.5 Fault 2: layer 4, on the other PE

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show route vrf BLUE 10.1.1.0/24
% Network not in table
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show bgp vpnv4 unicast rd 65000:101 10.1.1.0/24
Paths: (0 available, no best path)

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show bgp vpnv4 unicast vrf BLUE 10.1.1.0/24 detail
  Advertised to peers (in unique update groups):
    2001:db8:100::6
      Extended community: RT:65000:110
  • PE6 sends the return traffic. Thus we examine the layers on PE6, for the prefix of CE-A.
  • PE6 has no route to the subnet of CE-A in BLUE.
  • BGP has no path for it.
  • But PE1 shows that it advertised the route to PE6, with route target 65000:110. PE6 imports 65000:100. One digit is different.
  • PE6 received the route, found no VRF that matches, and discarded it. We set the export on PE1 back to 65000:100, and the fault was repaired.
  • The finding: when a ping fails, examine the two directions. Examine the PE where the reply stops, also when the customer who reports the problem is on the other side.

18.6 Fault 3: one VRF dead

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 3
Success rate is 0 percent (0/3)
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf BLUE 10.1.6.2 source 10.1.1.1 count 2
Success rate is 100 percent (2/2), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/2 ms
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf RED 10.2.6.2 source 10.2.1.1 count 2
Success rate is 100 percent (2/2), round-trip min/avg/max = 3/5/7 ms

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show bgp vpnv4 unicast vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
       SID Locator: fcbb:bb00:66::/48, RIB metric: inaccessible
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show cef vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32
    unresolved
    SRv6 H.Encaps.Red SID-list {fcbb:bb00:66:e008::}
    0     Y   recursive                 drop
  • Fault 3. Only GREEN does not operate.
  • GREEN fails.
  • BLUE and RED to the same PE go through. Thus PE6 is reachable, and its main locator operates.
  • Layer 4 for GREEN: the locator of the SID is fcbb:bb00:66::/48. It is not the MAIN locator of PE6, and it is inaccessible.
  • CEF shows unresolved and drop. This is the same as fault A in Episode 3, but for one VRF only.

18.7 Fault 3: down to layers 1 and 2

Router / tool: PE6

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show segment-routing srv6 locator
FA128                 1        128   fcbb:bb01:6::/48          Up       U
MAIN                  2        0     fcbb:bb00:6::/48          Up       U
TEST                  3        0     fcbb:bb00:66::/48         Up       U

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show isis segment-routing srv6 locators
FA128                 1        128   fcbb:bb01:6::/48          Active
MAIN                  2        0     fcbb:bb00:6::/48          Active
TEST                  3        0     fcbb:bb00:66::/48         Inactive

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show bgp vpnv4 unicast vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
    SRv6-VPN SID: fcbb:bb00:66:e008::/64
    Alloc Mode/Locator ID: per-vrf/3
  • Inaccessible points to layer 2. Thus we go to the owner, PE6.
  • Layer 1 shows a third locator, TEST. It is up locally.
  • Layer 2: IS-IS knows the locator, but shows it as inactive. Nobody added it under IS-IS. Thus the other routers cannot reach it.
  • The BGP configuration of GREEN allocates from it, locator ID 3. This is an incomplete change. Somebody made a new locator and moved a VRF to it, but did not do the IGP step.
  • We moved GREEN back to MAIN, and the fault was repaired. During the change, for approximately forty seconds, PE1 used the old SID, and PE6 had already removed it.
  • A change of SID is also an outage. Plan it.

18.8 Fault 3: the configuration changes

Router / tool: PE6

! Step 1, on PE6: a new locator, and RED allocates from it
segment-routing srv6 locators locator TEST
 micro-segment behavior unode psp-usd
 prefix fcbb:bb00:66::/48
router bgp 65000 vrf RED address-family ipv4 unicast
 segment-routing srv6 locator TEST
! (the locator is NOT added under router isis: the missing step)

! Step 2, on PE6: RED goes back to MAIN, and GREEN moves to TEST
router bgp 65000 vrf RED address-family ipv4 unicast
 segment-routing srv6 locator MAIN
router bgp 65000 vrf GREEN address-family ipv4 unicast
 segment-routing srv6 locator TEST
  • These are the configuration changes of fault 3, all on PE6. We made them in two steps.
  • Step 1 creates a locator TEST, and RED IPv4 allocates its service SID from it.
  • Look at the last line. The locator is not added under IS-IS. This is the missing step. Thus no other router has a route to it.
  • Step 2 puts RED back on MAIN, and moves GREEN to TEST. Now only GREEN depends on the broken locator. The twist after this page explains why RED survived in step 1.

18.9 Fault 3: the repair

Router / tool: PE6

! Repair 1, on PE6: GREEN back to MAIN
router bgp 65000 vrf GREEN address-family ipv4 unicast
 segment-routing srv6 locator MAIN

! Repair 2, on PE6: remove the unused locator
segment-routing srv6 locators
 no locator TEST
  • Now the repair, also on PE6, in two steps.
  • Repair 1 moves GREEN back to the MAIN locator. The traffic recovers after the new SID is advertised.
  • Repair 2 removes the locator TEST, which nobody uses. Do this last. Remove a locator only after no VRF allocates from it.

18.10 Fault 4: hidden until a link fails

Before the change:
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route ipv6 fcbb:bb01:6::/48
    fe80::5454:ff:fe66:75e1, from 2001:db8:100::6, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0, Backup (TI-LFA)
    fe80::5454:ff:fec1:58eb, from 2001:db8:100::6, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1, Protected

After the change on P2 and P4, everything still passes:
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route ipv6 fcbb:bb01:6::/48
    fe80::5454:ff:fec1:58eb, from 2001:db8:100::6, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1
  • Fault 4 is the most difficult type. When we make the change, nothing fails. We removed Flex-Algo 128 from P2 and P4. An engineer can make this change to make those routers simpler. RED IPv6 uses the algorithm 128 locator, and it continued to operate.
  • Before the change, the route on PE1 to the algorithm 128 locator of PE6 was protected, with a TI-LFA backup through P2.
  • After the change, there is one path and no protection. The algorithm 128 topology became one line: PE1, P3, P5, PE6. All pings still went through.
  • Only layer 2 showed the problem, and only when we compared it with the reference.

18.11 Fault 4: the link fails

P3: interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1 shutdown   (the link to P5)

CE-A:~$ sudo ping6 -c 3 -W 2 -I 2001:db8:c:201::2 2001:db8:c:206::2
3 packets transmitted, 0 packets received, 100% packet loss

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route ipv6 fcbb:bb01:6::/48
% Network not in table
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show cef vrf RED ipv6 2001:db8:c:206::/64
    unresolved
    0     Y   recursive                 drop

BLUE: 2 of 2.  RED IPv4: 2 of 2 (the PCE recomputed: latency 15000, via PE6's node SID).
  • Now the topology event: the link from P3 to P5 fails.
  • We shut it on P3.
  • RED IPv6 does not operate.
  • Layer 2: the algorithm 128 locator is not there. P2 and P4 are not in the algorithm, thus the algorithm has no other path. Layer 3 shows unresolved and drop.
  • All the other services continue. BLUE uses algorithm 0. RED IPv4 uses the policy from the PCE, and the PCE calculated a new path on the remaining links.
  • The customer that paid for the special path is the customer that lost service. We set the link and the algorithm back, and the route was protected again.

18.12 The four configuration changes

! fault 1, on P2: a smaller IPv6 MTU toward P4
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1
 ipv6 mtu 1400
! fault 2, on PE1: a different export route target
vrf BLUE
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  export route-target
   no 65000:100
   65000:110
! fault 3, on PE6: a locator that IS-IS does not advertise
! (full configuration on the Fault 3 pages)
locator TEST  prefix fcbb:bb00:66::/48
router bgp 65000 vrf RED address-family ipv4 unicast
 segment-routing srv6 locator TEST
! fault 4, on P2 and P4
router isis CORE
 no flex-algo 128
  • Here are the four changes, as the answer key. You can repeat each one in your lab, and then find it with the five layers, before you look at this page.
  • Fault 1: on P2, the IPv6 MTU of the link toward P4 is 1400.
  • Fault 2: on PE1, the export route target of BLUE IPv4 changes from 65000:100 to 65000:110.
  • Fault 3: on PE6, RED allocates its service SID from a new locator. IS-IS does not advertise this locator.
  • Fault 4: on P2 and P4, we remove Flex-Algo 128. The service is fine until a link fails.

Ep19 · The Security Boundary, and Scale

19.1 The untrusted port

interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/4
 description UNTRUSTED outside
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:ffff:1::1/64

Outside host, on CE-A's third port:
CE-A:~$ sudo ip -6 addr add 2001:db8:ffff:1::2/64 dev eth2
CE-A:~$ sudo ip -6 route add fcbb:bb00::/31 via 2001:db8:ffff:1::1
CE-A:~$ sudo ip -6 route add 2001:db8:100::/64 via 2001:db8:ffff:1::1
  • Now the test. The port for the Layer 2 service in Episode 14 becomes a port that is not trusted, in the global table of PE1. In a real network, it can be an internet peering, a management network or a customer that makes mistakes.
  • It has a plain IPv6 address, with no VRF.
  • The outside host gets an address on that link.
  • The host also gets routes to the two SID blocks and to the loopbacks, through PE1. A real attacker does not need these routes. A default route does the same.

19.2 Before: the outside reaches the core

Router / tool: CE-A

CE-A:~$ sudo ping6 -c 2 -W 2 fcbb:bb00:6::
64 bytes from 2001:db8:100::6: seq=0 ttl=61 time=3.693 ms
CE-A:~$ sudo ping6 -c 2 -W 2 fcbb:bb00:4::
64 bytes from 2001:db8:100::4: seq=0 ttl=62 time=1.757 ms
CE-A:~$ sudo ping6 -c 2 -W 2 fcbb:bb00:6:e000::
64 bytes from 2001:db8:100::6: seq=0 ttl=61 time=1.801 ms
CE-A:~$ sudo ping6 -c 2 -W 2 fcbb:bb00:6:e004::
64 bytes from 2001:db8:100::6: seq=0 ttl=61 time=1.656 ms
  • There is no filter yet. The outside host tries the SIDs of the core.
  • The node SID of PE6 gets a reply, from the loopback of PE6.
  • The node SID of P4, a transit router, gets a reply.
  • One of the adjacency SIDs of PE6 gets a reply.
  • The BLUE service SID also gets a reply. From outside the network, an unknown person touched the door to the VRF of a customer.
  • As Episode 17 showed, a ping does not cause a VRF lookup. But it shows that packets from outside arrive at the SID. A host that also makes the inner packet needs nothing more. We did not do that attack. It was not necessary.

19.3 Before, on the wire

Router / tool: tshark

$ tshark -r <capture file> -Y "icmpv6.type == 128 or icmpv6.type == 129" \
    -T fields -e ipv6.src -e ipv6.dst -e icmpv6.type | sort | uniq -c
# PE1 to P2: requests and replies
  2  2001:db8:ffff:1::2   fcbb:bb00:6::         128
  2  2001:db8:ffff:1::2   fcbb:bb00:4::         128
  2  2001:db8:100::6      2001:db8:ffff:1::2    129
  2  2001:db8:100::4      2001:db8:ffff:1::2    129
# P4 to PE6
  2  2001:db8:ffff:1::2   fcbb:bb00:6::         128
  2  2001:db8:100::6      2001:db8:ffff:1::2    129
  • This is the capture from that test. We read each file with tshark. Type 128 is a request, and type 129 is a reply.
  • On the link PE1 to P2, the requests of the outside host went into the core with no change, to the SIDs. The loopbacks of the routers replied.
  • The same request arrived at PE6. Nothing at the edge stopped a packet from outside the domain to an instruction in the domain.

19.4 What the platform lists

Router / tool: PE6

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show segment-routing srv6 manager
  Security rules:
    SEC-1
    SEC-2
    SEC-3
  • Does the router protect itself? The SRv6 manager shows security rules.
  • These are SEC-1 to SEC-3. The names come from RFC 8754, section 5.1. It describes filters at the domain edge and on SR nodes.
  • The list shows what the software supports. Our test shows the result without our filter: each SID replied to the outside host. A rule in the list is not a configured rule. Episode 14 gave the same finding about capabilities.

19.5 The boundary ACL

ipv6 access-list SRV6-BOUNDARY-IN
 10 deny ipv6 any fcbb:bb00::/31 log
 20 deny ipv6 any any routing log
 30 permit ipv6 any any
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/4
 ipv6 access-group SRV6-BOUNDARY-IN ingress
  • The repair is an access list on each interface that faces outside the SR domain.
  • Line 10: no packet from outside can go to the SID space. One slash 31 prefix includes the two blocks: fcbb:bb00 for algorithm 0 and fcbb:bb01 for algorithm 128. This is an advantage of blocks that are next to each other.
  • Line 20: no packet with a routing header can go in. On this release, the ACL did not accept routing-type 4. It accepted the general routing keyword.
  • All other packets are permitted.
  • We apply the ACL inbound on the port that is not trusted.

19.6 After: the door is shut

Router / tool: CE-A

CE-A:~$ sudo ping6 -c 2 -W 2 -I 2001:db8:ffff:1::2 fcbb:bb00:6::
2 packets transmitted, 0 packets received, 100% packet loss
CE-A:~$ sudo ping6 -c 2 -W 2 -I 2001:db8:ffff:1::2 fcbb:bb00:4::
2 packets transmitted, 0 packets received, 100% packet loss
CE-A:~$ sudo ping6 -c 2 -W 2 -I 2001:db8:ffff:1::2 fcbb:bb00:6:e000::
2 packets transmitted, 0 packets received, 100% packet loss
CE-A:~$ sudo ping6 -c 2 -W 2 -I 2001:db8:ffff:1::2 fcbb:bb00:6:e004::
2 packets transmitted, 0 packets received, 100% packet loss
CE-A:~$ sudo ping6 -c 2 -W 2 -I 2001:db8:ffff:1::2 2001:db8:100::6
2 packets transmitted, 2 packets received, 0% packet loss
  • We do the same tests with the ACL.
  • The four SIDs get no reply.
  • The loopback of PE6 still replies. The boundary stops only the SID space. Usual reachability does not change.
  • Look at the -I option. Without it, the outside host used a different address as the source. PE6 had no route back to that address, thus the loopback ping also failed. When a test fails, examine the source address before you blame the filter.

19.7 After, on the wire

Router / tool: tshark

$ tshark -r <capture file> -Y "icmpv6.type == 128" -T fields -e ipv6.src -e ipv6.dst | sort | uniq -c
# outside host to PE1, on the port that is not trusted
  2  2001:db8:ffff:1::2   fcbb:bb00:4::
  2  2001:db8:ffff:1::2   fcbb:bb00:6::
  1  2001:db8:ffff:1::2   fcbb:bb00:6:e000::
# PE1 to P2
(no echo request)
  • Did the ACL drop the packets? We use captures to see this, with the same command.
  • The requests arrived at the port of PE1 that is not trusted.
  • None of them appeared on the core link of PE1. Thus PE1 dropped them at the edge.
  • On this platform, the deny counters of the ACL showed no matches. Verify the filter with a packet from outside and a capture inside. Do not use a counter as your only evidence.

19.8 Planning the SID space for the boundary

Router / tool: PE6

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show segment-routing srv6 manager
  SRv6 Operational Mode:
    Micro-segment:
      SID Base Block: fcbb:bb00::/24

Blocks in use:     fcbb:bb00::/32 (algorithm 0)   fcbb:bb01::/32 (algorithm 128)
Our ACL line:      deny ipv6 any fcbb:bb00::/31
Whole base block:  deny ipv6 any fcbb:bb00::/24
  • One more design point: how large must the deny prefix be?
  • The manager shows the micro-SID base block: fcbb:bb00::/24. All the blocks that this router can use are in it.
  • This lab uses two SID blocks, and our ACL line includes only those two.
  • If you deny all the base block, you also include each block that you add later. This can be another algorithm, or a migration block in Module 6.
  • The small prefix is precise. With the large prefix, you do not forget a block when the network grows. Select one, and record the reason.

19.9 Scale: the numbers on PE6

Router / tool: PE6

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show segment-routing srv6 manager
      uSID LIB Range:
        LIB Start   : 0xe000
        ELIB Start  : 0xfe00
Summary:
  Number of Locators: 2 (2 operational)
  Number of SIDs: 14 (0 stale)
  Max SID resources: 64000
  Number of free SID resources: 63986
    Block fcbb:bb00::/32:
        Number of SIDs free: 7671
        Max SIDs: 7680
  Max Locators: 16
  • Now scale. The layer 1 command from Episode 17 shows the numbers.
  • The local SID range starts at e000 and stops before fe00. All the functions in this lab came from this range: e004, e007, e00b. They are local, and each router uses the same values again, as Episode 16 showed.
  • PE6 uses 14 SIDs from 64000 resources.
  • Each block has 7680 SIDs. This is the size of the range from e000 to fdff. Thus the real limit for each locator is the local range, not the total.
  • The maximum is 16 locators.

Ep20 · From LDP and MPLS VPN to SRv6

20.1 The legacy configuration on PE1

interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
 ipv4 address 10.12.0.0 255.255.255.254
router isis CORE
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  metric-style wide
 interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
  address-family ipv4 unicast
   metric 10
router bgp 65000
 neighbor 10.0.0.6
  remote-as 65000
  update-source Loopback0
  address-family vpnv4 unicast
mpls ldp
 router-id 10.0.0.1
 interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
  • This is the MPLS configuration on PE1, with some lines removed. The other routers have the same pattern.
  • There are IPv4 addresses on the core links.
  • IPv4 is in the same IS-IS instance, with the same metrics as IPv6.
  • There is a VPNv4 session to the IPv4 loopback of PE6.
  • LDP is on the core interfaces. GREEN has no SRv6 allocation on any router.

20.2 GREEN on MPLS

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show mpls ldp neighbor brief
10.0.0.2:0         N   N    00:01:26    1     0     4     0     14     0
10.0.0.3:0         N   N    00:01:24    1     0     4     0     14     0

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show bgp vpnv4 unicast vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
    10.0.0.6 (metric 30) from 10.0.0.6 (10.0.0.6), if-handle 0x00000000
      Received Label 24000

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show cef vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
    next hop 10.0.0.6/32 via 24011/0/21
     next hop 10.12.0.1/32 GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0 labels imposed {24009 24000}
  • This is GREEN on MPLS, as an older network shows it.
  • There are LDP sessions to P2 and P3.
  • The GREEN route from PE6 has next hop 10.0.0.6 and a real MPLS label, 24000.
  • CEF pushes two labels. 24009 is the LDP label to PE6, and 24000 is the VPN label. Compare this with Episode 13: one IPv6 header with one SID.

20.3 Both worlds on one wire

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 3
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/3 ms
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf BLUE 10.100.6.6 source 10.100.1.1 count 2
Success rate is 100 percent (2/2), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/3 ms

$ tshark -r <capture file> -Y "mpls or ipv6.nxt == 4" -T fields -e frame.len -e mpls.label -e ipv6.dst -e icmp.type
# PE1 to P2        122   24009,24000          GREEN request, MPLS
#                  154   fcbb:bb00:6:e004::   BLUE request, SRv6
# P2 to P4         122   24009,24000          GREEN request
#                  154   fcbb:bb00:6:e004::   BLUE request
# P4 to PE6        118   24000                GREEN request, top label popped
#                  154   fcbb:bb00:6:e004::   BLUE request
  • We captured on three core links while PE1 sent 100-byte pings to GREEN and to BLUE. We read each file with tshark.
  • Both pings work. When they leave PE1, GREEN has two labels, 122 bytes. BLUE has an IPv6 header, 154 bytes.
  • It is the same on the link from P2 to P4.
  • On the last link, GREEN has no top label. P4 removed it: this is penultimate-hop popping. BLUE does not change from end to end. The two technologies use each router and each link, and they do not affect each other.
  • Look at the sizes. The SRv6 packet is 32 bytes larger than the MPLS packet with two labels. When GREEN moves, it loses 32 bytes of MTU. Examine this before you migrate, with the method of Episode 7.

20.4 Reading the labels hop by hop

Router / tool: tshark

$ tshark -r <capture file> -Y "mpls" -T fields -e frame.len -e mpls.label -e icmp.type
# GREEN request, from PE1 to PE6
PE1 to P2     122   24009,24000
P2 to P4      122   24009,24000
P4 to PE6     118   24000          (the top label was popped by P4)
# GREEN reply, from PE6 to PE1
P4 to PE6     122   24001,24000
P2 to P4      122   24000,24000
PE1 to P2     118   24000          (the top label was already popped)
  • We look at MPLS again, because it shows what SRv6 removes.
  • PE1 sends 24009 on top. This is the label of P2 for PE6. Below it is 24000, the VPN label of PE6.
  • P2 replaces the top label with the label of P4 for PE6. This label is also 24009. Each router has its own labels. The equal numbers are a coincidence.
  • P4 removes the top label before PE6.
  • The replies show the same pattern in the opposite direction, and PE6 starts with 24001. Each router keeps a label table for each PE. With SRv6, the transit routers forwarded one IPv6 destination that did not change. They used their usual routing table.

20.5 Step 1: PE6 moves first

router bgp 65000
 vrf GREEN
  address-family ipv4 unicast
   segment-routing srv6
    locator MAIN
    alloc mode per-vrf

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show bgp vpnv4 unicast vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
    10.0.0.6 (metric 30) from 10.0.0.6 (10.0.0.6), if-handle 0x00000000
      Received Label 0xe0080
       SID Locator: fcbb:bb00:6::/48, RIB metric: 31
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show cef vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
    SRv6 H.Encaps.Red SID-list {fcbb:bb00:6:e008::}
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 3
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 1/3/6 ms
  • Step 1. Only PE6 changes.
  • PE6 allocates an SRv6 SID for GREEN. These are the same five lines as for BLUE in Episode 12.
  • On PE1, the GREEN route now arrives with a SID. Look at the next hop: it is still 10.0.0.6, the IPv4 session. PE6 advertised the SID on the two sessions, and PE1 selected the path from the IPv4 session.
  • This is not important. The SID selects the encapsulation. The session does not.
  • CEF now encapsulates with the GREEN SID of PE6.
  • GREEN operates.

20.6 Step 1: one route, two paths

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show bgp vpnv4 unicast rd 65000:306 10.30.6.6/32
Paths: (2 available, best #1)
  Path #1: Received by speaker 0
    10.0.0.6 (metric 30) from 10.0.0.6 (10.0.0.6)
      Received Label 0xe0080
      Origin incomplete, metric 0, localpref 100, valid, internal, best, group-best
  Path #2: Received by speaker 0
    2001:db8:100::6 (metric 30) from 2001:db8:100::6 (10.0.0.6)
      Received Label 0xe0080
      Origin incomplete, metric 0, localpref 100, valid, internal
  • Why did PE1 use the path from the IPv4 session? This is the route from PE6 on PE1, before the import into GREEN.
  • The same route has two paths, one from each session.
  • Path 1 is over IPv4, with the SID. It is the best path.
  • Path 2 is over IPv6, with the same SID. All the attributes in the output are equal. Thus the last BGP tie-break rules selected the path.
  • The two paths go to the same SID and make the same packet. During a migration, two sessions are usual. Know which path is best, and why.

20.7 Step 1 on the wire: half and half

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 3
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 1/3/6 ms

$ tshark -r step1-PE1-P2.pcap -Y "mpls or ipv6.nxt == 4" \
    -T fields -e frame.len -e mpls.label -e ipv6.dst -e ip.src | sort | uniq -c
  3   154                       fcbb:bb00:6:e008::   10.30.1.1    PE1 to PE6, requests: SRv6
  3   118   24000                                    10.30.6.6    PE6 to PE1, replies: MPLS
  • The wire shows the result of step 1, on the link PE1 to P2. The ping works.
  • The requests from PE1 to PE6 are SRv6, because their egress, PE6, moved.
  • The replies from PE6 to PE1 are still MPLS, because their egress, PE1, did not move. One customer and one ping use two technologies, and the ping operates. One end can move first.

20.8 Step 2: PE1 follows

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 3
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 1/3/6 ms
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf BLUE 10.100.6.6 source 10.100.1.1 count 2
Success rate is 100 percent (2/2), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/3 ms

$ tshark -r step2-PE1-P2.pcap -Y "ipv6.nxt == 4" -T fields -e frame.len -e ipv6.dst -e ip.src | sort | uniq -c
  3   154   fcbb:bb00:6:e008::   10.30.1.1     GREEN request
  3   154   fcbb:bb00:1:e00a::   10.30.6.6     GREEN reply
  2   154   fcbb:bb00:6:e004::   10.100.1.1    BLUE request
  2   154   fcbb:bb00:1:e004::   10.100.6.6    BLUE reply
  • Step 2: we configure the same five lines on PE1. Then we run the same two pings.
  • The GREEN requests go to the GREEN SID of PE6, as before.
  • Now the replies go to the new GREEN SID of PE1, e00a. The two directions are SRv6.
  • BLUE did not change. After this step, the GREEN and BLUE pings went through.

20.9 Rollback of step 1

router bgp 65000
 vrf GREEN
  address-family ipv4 unicast
   no segment-routing srv6

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show bgp vpnv4 unicast vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
    10.0.0.6 (metric 30) from 10.0.0.6 (10.0.0.6), if-handle 0x00000000
      Received Label 24000
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show cef vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
     next hop 10.12.0.1/32 GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0 labels imposed {24009 24000}
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 3
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/4/6 ms
  • Now the test that each change plan needs: can we go back? PE1 had already moved, and we rolled back step 1 on PE6.
  • One line on PE6 removes the SRv6 allocation of GREEN.
  • PE1 receives label 24000 again.
  • CEF uses the two labels again. LDP was still in operation, thus the transport label was ready.
  • GREEN goes through. On the wire, the requests were MPLS again. The replies stayed SRv6, because we did not roll back PE1. The two directions use different technologies again, but in the opposite way.
  • We applied step 1 again, and the two directions were SRv6 again.

20.10 Rollback on the wire

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 3
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/4/6 ms

$ tshark -r rollback-PE6-PE1-P2.pcap -Y "mpls or ipv6.nxt == 4" \
    -T fields -e frame.len -e mpls.label -e ipv6.dst -e ip.src | sort | uniq -c
  3   122   24009,24000                               10.30.1.1    GREEN request: MPLS again
  3   154                       fcbb:bb00:1:e00a::   10.30.6.6    GREEN reply: still SRv6
  • This is the capture during the rollback. The ping works.
  • The requests to PE6 are MPLS again, with two labels, because PE6 withdrew its SID.
  • The replies to PE1 stay SRv6, to the GREEN SID of PE1. The rule is also true in the opposite direction: each direction follows its egress, when the egress moves forward or back.

20.11 Step 3: remove the legacy

router bgp 65000
 no neighbor 10.0.0.6
no mpls ldp                                 (on all six routers)

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show bgp vpnv4 unicast vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
    2001:db8:100::6 (metric 30) from 2001:db8:100::6 (10.0.0.6), if-handle 0x00000000
      Received Label 0xe0080
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show mpls forwarding
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show mpls ldp neighbor brief
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 3
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/3 ms
  • Step 3: remove the MPLS configuration, in sequence.
  • First, remove the IPv4 BGP session on the two PEs.
  • Then remove LDP on all six routers.
  • The GREEN route now comes from the IPv6 loopback of PE6, with its SID.
  • The MPLS forwarding table is empty, and there are no LDP neighbors.
  • GREEN and BLUE go through. On the wire, GREEN is SRv6 in the two directions. The migration is complete.

Ep21 · From SR-MPLS to SRv6

21.1 Step 1: SR-MPLS configuration

On every router, here P2:
router isis CORE
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  segment-routing mpls
 interface Loopback0
  address-family ipv4 unicast
   prefix-sid index 2

On PE1, mirrored on PE6:
router bgp 65000
 neighbor 10.0.0.6
  remote-as 65000
  update-source Loopback0
  address-family vpnv4 unicast
 vrf GREEN
  address-family ipv4 unicast
   no segment-routing srv6
  • The IPv4 core from Episode 20 remains. This time, it has no LDP.
  • We enable segment routing for MPLS under the IS-IS IPv4 address family.
  • Each loopback gets a prefix SID index. P2 uses 2. PE6 uses 6.
  • The PEs use an IPv4 BGP session for VPNv4 routes with labels.
  • GREEN has no SRv6 allocation. Thus it uses MPLS labels.

21.2 Step 1: the result

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show isis segment-routing label table
Label         Prefix                   Algorithm    Interface
16006         10.0.0.6/32              SPF

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show mpls forwarding prefix 10.0.0.6/32
Local  Outgoing    Prefix             Outgoing     Next Hop        Bytes
16006  16006       SR Pfx (idx 6)     Gi0/0/0/0    10.12.0.1       872

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show cef vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
    next hop 10.0.0.6/32 via 16006/0/21
     next hop 10.12.0.1/32 GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0 labels imposed {16006 24000}

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 3
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/2 ms
  • This is the result on PE1.
  • The loopback of PE6 has label 16006. The default label block starts at 16000. Add the index of PE6, which is 6.
  • PE1 replaces label 16006 with label 16006. The values match because these routers use the same SRGB. The advertised index has domain-wide meaning.
  • GREEN packets get two labels. Label 16006 reaches PE6. Label 24000 identifies the VPN service on PE6.
  • The ping receives replies.

21.3 Step 1: on the wire

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 3
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/2 ms

$ tshark -r <capture file> -Y "mpls" -T fields -e frame.len -e mpls.label -e ip.src
# PE1 to P2
122   16006,24000   10.30.1.1    GREEN request
118   24000         10.30.6.6    GREEN reply
# P2 to P4
122   16006,24000   10.30.1.1    GREEN request
122   16001,24000   10.30.6.6    GREEN reply
  • We examine two core links, with a GREEN ping from PE1, and we read each file with tshark.
  • At PE1, label 16006 is above label 24000. The replies carry the label 24000 only, because the router before PE1 removed the top label.
  • On the next link, the top label is still 16006. These routers use the same SRGB and associate index 6 with PE6. LDP allocated labels independently in Episode 20. The replies carry label 16001 for PE1.

21.4 Step 2: move GREEN to SRv6

On PE6 and PE1:
router bgp 65000
 vrf GREEN
  address-family ipv4 unicast
   segment-routing srv6
    locator MAIN
    alloc mode per-vrf

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show cef vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
10.30.6.6/32, version 19, SRv6 Headend
    SRv6 H.Encaps.Red SID-list {fcbb:bb00:6:e008::}
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 3
Success rate is 100 percent (3/3), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/3 ms
  • The migration uses the same five lines as Episode 20.
  • We configure SRv6 allocation for GREEN on each PE. Episode 20 demonstrated separate PE migrations. The same rule applies here: the egress decides the encapsulation.
  • CEF now encapsulates GREEN with the SID of PE6.
  • GREEN receives ping replies.

21.5 Step 2: on the wire

Router / tool: tshark

$ tshark -r <capture file> -Y "ipv6.nxt == 4" -T fields -e frame.len -e ipv6.dst -e ip.src
# PE1 to P2
154   fcbb:bb00:6:e008::   10.30.1.1    GREEN request
154   fcbb:bb00:1:e00a::   10.30.6.6    GREEN reply
# P2 to P4
154   fcbb:bb00:6:e008::   10.30.1.1    GREEN request
154   fcbb:bb00:1:e00a::   10.30.6.6    GREEN reply
  • These are the same two links after migration, read with the same command.
  • Both directions use SRv6. Each destination is the GREEN SID of the egress PE. These customer packets have no MPLS labels.
  • P2 forwards the packet without changing its destination, as with BLUE in Episode 13.

21.6 Step 3: who still uses label 16006?

Before the move:
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show mpls forwarding prefix 10.0.0.6/32
Local  Outgoing    Prefix             Outgoing     Next Hop        Bytes
16006  16006       SR Pfx (idx 6)     Gi0/0/0/0    10.12.0.1       872

After the move, GREEN on SRv6:
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show mpls forwarding prefix 10.0.0.6/32
Local  Outgoing    Prefix             Outgoing     Next Hop        Bytes
16006  16006       SR Pfx (idx 6)     Gi0/0/0/0    10.12.0.1       1415
  • GREEN uses SRv6 now. Does SR-MPLS still carry traffic?
  • Before migration, the label entry for PE6 showed 872 switched bytes.
  • After migration, the counter showed 1415 bytes. Some traffic still used label 16006. We tested the cause later. During sixty seconds with no customer traffic, the counter increased by 99 bytes.
  • The capture showed two labeled packets for the IPv4 BGP session to 10.0.0.6. A BGP keepalive was 59 bytes. A TCP acknowledgement was 40 bytes. Together, they account for the 99-byte increase.
  • After we removed that session, the counter stopped increasing. The old transport still carried control traffic. Identify all traffic that uses the old transport before you remove it.

21.7 Step 3: remove the IPv4 VPN session

Router / tool: PE1

! On PE1. PE6 does the same with neighbor 10.0.0.1
router bgp 65000
 no neighbor 10.0.0.6

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show mpls forwarding prefix 10.0.0.6/32     (00:28:51)
16006  16006       SR Pfx (idx 6)     Gi0/0/0/0    10.12.0.1       1251

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show mpls forwarding prefix 10.0.0.6/32     (00:29:53)
16006  16006       SR Pfx (idx 6)     Gi0/0/0/0    10.12.0.1       1251

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 2
Success rate is 100 percent (2/2), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/2 ms
  • Step 3 removes the last user of label 16006: the IPv4 VPN session.
  • On PE1, we remove the neighbor 10.0.0.6. PE6 removes the neighbor 10.0.0.1.
  • Now we read the counter of label 16006 twice, about one minute apart. It is 1251 both times. The counter stopped.
  • GREEN still works, over SRv6.

21.8 Step 4: remove SR-MPLS

Router / tool: PE1

! On every router, here PE1
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1(config)#no router isis CORE address-family ipv4 unicast
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1(config)#no router isis CORE interface Loopback0 address-family ipv4 unicast
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1(config)#no router isis CORE interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0 address-family ipv4 unicast
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1(config)#no router isis CORE interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1 address-family ipv4 unicast
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1(config)#commit

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show running-config router isis CORE
 (only SRv6 lines remain: segment-routing srv6, microloop avoidance)
  • Step 4 removes SR-MPLS. Do it last, and only after the counter stopped.
  • On each router, we remove the IPv4 address family from IS-IS, on the instance and on each interface. This also removes the prefix SIDs and segment routing for MPLS.
  • Then we commit.
  • The running configuration of IS-IS now has only the SRv6 lines.

Ep22 · From OSPF to IS-IS

22.1 The legacy IGP, added to every router

Router / tool: P3

router ospf LEGACY
 router-id 10.0.0.3
 area 0
  interface Loopback0
   passive enable
  interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
   cost 40
   network point-to-point
  interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/2
   cost 10
   network point-to-point
router ospfv3 LEGACY
 router-id 10.0.0.3
 area 0
  interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
   cost 40
  • All six routers run OSPF for IPv4 and OSPFv3 for IPv6. This is the configuration on P3.
  • We use area 0 and make the loopback passive.
  • The link costs match the IS-IS metrics. The lower links use 40. The other links use 10. We verify that both protocols select the same paths. Then the migration changes route ownership without changing those paths.
  • OSPFv3 uses the same link costs. The IS-IS configuration remains unchanged.

22.2 Two IGPs: who owns what

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show ospf neighbor
10.0.0.2        1     FULL/  -        00:00:37    10.12.0.1       GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
10.0.0.3        1     FULL/  -        00:00:37    10.13.0.1       GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route ipv6 2001:db8:100::6/128
  Known via "ospf LEGACY", distance 110, metric 30, type intra area
    fe80::5454:ff:fe66:75e1, from ::, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route ipv6 fcbb:bb00:6::/48
  Known via "isis CORE", distance 115, metric 31, SRv6-locator, type level-2
    fe80::5454:ff:fe66:75e1, from 2001:db8:100::6, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0, Protected
    fe80::5454:ff:fec1:58eb, from 2001:db8:100::6, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1, Backup (TI-LFA)

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show ospfv3 database | include fcbb
  • Which protocol supplies each route when both IGPs operate?
  • OSPF adjacencies show Full. IS-IS adjacencies also remain up.
  • OSPF supplies the selected loopback route for PE6. Both protocols know the prefix. OSPF has distance 110, which is lower than the IS-IS distance of 115. This selected route has one path and no backup.
  • IS-IS still supplies the locator route for PE6, with a TI-LFA backup. In this configuration, OSPF does not advertise the locator.
  • The OSPFv3 database has no SID block prefixes. A BLUE ping receives replies.

22.3 Step 1: prefer IS-IS everywhere

On every router:
router isis CORE
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  distance 100
 address-family ipv6 unicast
  distance 100

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route ipv6 2001:db8:100::6/128
  Known via "isis CORE", distance 100, metric 30, type level-2
    fe80::5454:ff:fe66:75e1, from 2001:db8:100::6, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0, Protected
    fe80::5454:ff:fec1:58eb, from 2001:db8:100::6, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1, Backup (TI-LFA)
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route ipv4 10.0.0.6/32
  Known via "isis CORE", distance 100, metric 30, labeled SR
  • Step 1 makes IS-IS preferred. Both protocols remain configured.
  • We set IS-IS distance 100 in both address families on all six routers. It is lower than the OSPF distance of 110. OSPF adjacencies remain Full, so its routes remain available.
  • IS-IS now supplies the selected loopback route for PE6. The route has TI-LFA protection.
  • The IPv4 loopback also uses IS-IS. It retains the SR-MPLS label from Episode 21. The service tests pass.
  • The IPv4 metric is 30. Under OSPFv2, it was 31 because OSPFv2 added the loopback interface cost of 1. Equal link costs did not produce equal totals. Compare total costs and selected paths before you rely on a mixed network.

22.4 Step 2: remove OSPF

On every router:
no router ospf LEGACY
no router ospfv3 LEGACY

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show ospf neighbor
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route ipv6 fcbb:bb00:6::/48
  Known via "isis CORE", distance 100, metric 31, SRv6-locator, type level-2
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf BLUE 10.100.6.6 source 10.100.1.1 count 2
Success rate is 100 percent (2/2), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/3/4 ms
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6 source 10.30.1.1 count 2
Success rate is 100 percent (2/2), round-trip min/avg/max = 3/3/4 ms
  • Step 2 removes OSPF.
  • We enter two lines on each router.
  • No OSPF neighbors remain. The selected routing table does not change because IS-IS already supplies these routes.
  • BLUE and GREEN receive replies. Step 1 changed route preference. Step 2 removes the unused protocol. This final removal should not change the selected paths.

Ep23 · What Changes on Hardware

23.1 The same command, on both

Router / tool: PE6

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show segment-routing srv6 manager
  Signaled parameters:
    Max-SL          : 3
    Max-End-Pop-SRH : 3
    Max-H-Insert    : 3 sids
    Max-H-Encap     : 3 sids
    Max-End-D       : 4
  Configurable parameters (under srv6):
    Encapsulation:
      Hop-Limit     : value=Yes, propagate=No
      Traffic-class : value=Yes, propagate=Yes
  Max Locators: 16
  Max SIDs: 64000
  • Run the same manager command on both platforms. This is the XRd output from Episode 17.
  • The output lists segments-left, insertion, encapsulation and decapsulation limits. IS-IS advertises these capabilities. A headend or PCE can use them when it constructs a path.
  • The output also describes header propagation. Hop limit propagation is disabled here. Traffic class propagation is available. Episode 13 measured the resulting DSCP behavior.
  • The resource limits appear below. Compare this output with the hardware output before you complete the design. Record the platform and release with each output.

Ep24 · Integrated experiment findings

24.1 What a findings line looks like

This is a condensed findings example, not a new measurement. The complete integrated experiment remains unverified.

- Largest tenant IP packet that passes is 1446 bytes (1500 minus 40 minus 14).
  One byte more and PE1 fragments the outer IPv6 packet; the far end does not
  deliver it and the ping fails. No error reaches the CE.

- The ACL counters showed no matches on the deny lines even though the traffic
  was dropped. Do not use the counters as proof here.

- ODN with sid-algorithm 128 through the PCE: stays down, SRv6 SIDs failed
  verification. Cisco's 25.x guide lists the case as not supported.
  • These examples show how to write a finding.
  • State the measured limit and the result one byte above it. Also state whether the customer received an error.
  • Describe an unexpected result directly. Explain how it changes the next test.
  • For a documented limitation, include the source and release. Keep the finding specific enough for another person to verify.
00

實驗記錄與截圖判讀

實驗與圖文記錄

這是一組 SRv6 的深度學習實驗，這裡記錄了每個實驗的過程，並且用 AI 製作成影片。

這是在 lab 上真實測試 SRv6，並非只看書本。每一個實驗：先帶入問題，接著測試，最後得到答案。

你可以在自己的 lab 上重現，簡報檔及圖文版記錄詳細過程，包括指令、設備設定檔，及實驗得到的輸出。

圖文記錄實驗過程，包括大量實驗的截圖，以及每個實驗步驟的指令、輸出及判讀。每章分開說明觀察結果、推論與下一項有效檢查。

起點知識與 lab 拓撲

需要具備 IPv6、IS-IS、BGP、MPLS VPN、routing table 與 VRF 的基本知識。附錄 A 說明 SRv6 名詞。指令範例使用 Cisco IOS XR。

PE 是連接客戶與核心的 provider edge router；P 是核心 router；CE 是客戶端設備。本實驗以 PE1 為一端、PE6 為另一端，P2–P5 位於核心。BLUE、RED、GREEN 是不同服務名稱，不是 packet header 中的固定欄位。

核心拓撲：link cost 與服務端點

實驗順序

階段 章節 實驗問題
建立模型 1–3 哪個節點執行哪個 SID？destination address 如何改變？
接上路由與服務 4–5 locator 從哪裡來？service SID 如何把 packet 送入正確 VRF？
計算封裝 6–7 核心實際承載什麼？為何大小上限改變？
驗證路徑與保護 8–10 故障後走哪裡？指定節點是否等於指定 link？
故障排除與遷移 11–12 哪個證據指出原因？什麼時候可以移除舊傳輸？

中英文版採用相同的章序與實驗編號；切換語言時會定位到相同主題。影片集數、圖片編號與章號是不同索引，圖說保留影片原始集數。

預測、觀察、解釋

  1. 預測：測試前記下預期的 packet header、表格、路徑或大小。
  2. 觀察：用指令、輸出與截圖檢查預測。
  3. 解釋：記錄改變之處、仍正常的狀態，以及支持原因的證據。

推演範例與附錄 B 提供判讀參考。操作前先確認每一步的起點條件。

沒有實驗環境時，也可以完成欄位判讀、路徑推演與大小計算。第 1 章的 L1 需要已建立的 L3VPN；從空白環境開始時，先理解流程，完成第 5 章後再回來操作 L1。

如何讀實驗截圖

每張圖都有 F 編號、影片集數與時間點。先確認圖中的設備與狀態，再找到正文要求比較的欄位，最後判斷這個欄位能證明什麼。HTML 版可點選圖片放大。

例如，F06 是正常狀態，F07 是 locator 故障。應比較 locator 可達性與 BGP 解析結果，而不是只看畫面是否有錯誤文字。F08 則是另一種分配故障，不能把它與 F07 視為同一個失敗原因。

58 張顯示圖片擷取自既有影片中的實驗輸出面板。影片會選取並排版指令輸出與 packet 資料。圖片中的英文保留原文；動態 SID 值只適用於當次紀錄。這次編寫沒有登入 router 重新實測。

實驗與證據的範圍

主要實驗使用六台 XRd vRouter，版本為 IOS XR 26.2.2，平台為 CML 2.10.0。部分補充實驗使用 IOS XR 26.1.1 的 XRv9000。這些結果不能證明實體硬體效能、容量或所有版本的支援範圍。

「既有實測」表示來源紀錄中的觀察；「計算範例」表示依已知條件推導的結果；「未實測」表示實驗沒有完成該項驗證。推演案例用來解釋這些資料，不代表新增了一輪實驗。

操作前先儲存基線，確認管理存取與還原方式。只在隔離的實驗網路加入故障。前置條件不成立時，先停在該步，記錄差異；不要用後續變更掩蓋前一個問題。每輪實驗都要還原並重新驗收。

正文的說明、圖表與影片截圖可直接用於學習。附錄 C、D 的檔案路徑供持有完整實驗資料的人查閱；它們不是公開下載連結。實際重建實驗仍需要相符的映像檔、節點定義與設定檔。

01

狀態、packet 與五個問題

實驗問題：先分清「送到哪裡」與「到達後做什麼」

核心拓撲：link cost 與服務端點

先把一個客戶 packet 的旅程分成三段：PE1 選擇服務並封裝；核心依外層 IPv6 位址轉送；PE6 執行 service SID，再交付客戶。這三段各需要不同狀態。若把它們混成一次查表，就無法解釋為什麼 locator 可達，客戶卻仍收不到資料。

觀察與判讀： 本章指出 PE1、P2、PE6 各自需要哪些狀態，並說明核心為何不需要客戶 VRF。

起點狀態： 先看懂流程即可。L1 是觀察既有服務的實驗；從空白環境開始時，完成第 5 章的 L3VPN 後再回來操作。

為何 SRv6 不只需要一條路由

客戶 packet 到達 PE1 時，destination address 是客戶位址。PE1 必須先識別客戶的 routing table，再選擇遠端服務和傳輸路徑。

SRv6 使用 IPv6 destination address 識別 segment。segment 可以識別節點、adjacency 或服務功能。入口 router 可以把多個壓縮 segment 放入同一個 destination address。

destination address 不是可任意執行的程式碼。router 會對符合條件的 local SID 執行已安裝的行為。一般中繼 router 則執行 IPv6 轉送。

以下五個問題貫穿整個實驗：

問題 必要資訊 首先檢查的證據
哪個節點接收 packet？ 可達的 locator IPv6 RIB 和 CEF
節點執行什麼動作？ local SID 行為 出口 SID 表
哪個客戶接收 payload？ service context BGP 屬性和 VRF
故障後還能使用哪條路徑？ 修復路徑 CEF 和故障期間的 packet
哪個機制選擇路徑？ policy 或 algorithm policy 狀態和實際路徑

哪些狀態仍然存在

使用 LDP 時，核心 router 維護標籤綁定和鄰居 session。使用 RSVP-TE 時，中間節點還要維護隧道狀態。原實驗沒有建立 RSVP-TE 實驗。

使用 SRv6 時，PE1 維護客戶路由和封裝指令。PE6 維護 local service SID 和客戶 routing table。核心 router 維護 locator 路由、local SID 和保護狀態。

因此，核心並非沒有狀態。一般中間節點不需要維護客戶路由，也不需要維護每條 SR Policy 的狀態。資源需求仍會隨拓撲和 local 功能增加。

「中繼」是 router 對某個 packet 所扮演的角色。destination address 屬於 PE6 時，P4 是中繼 router。destination address 與 P4 自己的 SID 相符時，P4 就是 segment endpoint。

同一個 packet，三種傳輸方式

下表使用 100-byte 客戶 IP packet。Ethernet header 為 14 bytes。算式不包含 VLAN 標籤和 FCS。

傳輸方式 新增的傳輸位元組 核心 frame 位元組
兩個標籤的 MPLS 8 122
兩個標籤的 SR-MPLS 8 122
一個外層 IPv6 header 的 SRv6 40 154

此 SRv6 範例比兩個標籤的範例多用 32 bytes。這個差值只適用於表中的封裝方式。額外標籤、SRH 或其他 header 會改變結果。

推演案例：用一個 BLUE packet 串起三個節點

CE-A 的 packet 先到 PE1。PE1 在客戶 VRF 查閱目的網路，選出遠端服務並加入外層 IPv6 封裝。P2 看到的是外層 destination address，因此只需知道如何到達 PE6 locator。PE6 收到符合 service SID 的 packet 後，移除外層封裝，再以內層 destination address 查 BLUE。

讀圖順序： 從 F01 找出 P2 沒有客戶 VRF 的證據，再從 F02 找出 PE1 的客戶服務狀態。兩張圖放在一起，說明服務狀態集中在哪裡；它們不表示核心完全沒有狀態。

先想一想： 若 P2 有 PE6 locator 路由，而 PE6 沒有客戶路由，packet 是否仍能完成交付？先指出失敗的查表位置。

從證據推理：新增客戶時，哪些狀態必須改變？

在 PE1 與 PE6 新增一個 VRF，但不變更核心拓撲及 locator 規劃。哪些 router 需要新增客戶路由？

先預測結果，再展開比較判讀

PE 需要客戶路由與 service SID。Transit P router 仍依 locator 轉送。不執行客戶 BGP，不代表 P router 完全沒有狀態。

請分開比較 transport state 與 service state。即使客戶數不變，新增核心 adjacency 仍可能增加 local SID。

L1 — 建立狀態紀錄

起點狀態： 使用 L5 已驗收的 L3VPN 狀態。本實驗先讀取狀態，不變更設定。

在指定的 router 或工具執行指令。提示字元與輸出是證據，不要當成指令貼上。

設定區塊須在 configuration mode 輸入。完成一項變更後先 commit，再執行對應檢查。讀取結果後才進行下一項。

傳送測試流量前，先在指定 link 啟動擷取。核對 packet 方向、位址與 header 欄位。

輸出節錄省略無關行。動態 SID 與計數器可不同。只有設定區塊，不代表驗收成功。

階段 · Ep01 — 指令與結果
1.1 · What P2 actually holds

router／工具：P2

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:P2#show bgp summary
% BGP instance 'default' not active

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:P2#show route vrf all summary
VRF: **iid
connected                        0          0          0           0
Total                            0          0          0           0

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:P2#show segment-routing srv6 locator
Name                  ID       Algo  Prefix                    Status   Flags
FA128                 1        128   fcbb:bb01:2::/48          Up       U
MAIN                  2        0     fcbb:bb00:2::/48          Up       U

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:P2#show segment-routing srv6 manager | include Number of SIDs
  Number of SIDs: 12 (0 stale)
  • 現在我們檢查完成後實驗裡的 P2。這個實驗網路的所有服務都經過它。
  • P2 上沒有執行 BGP。
  • 沒有任何客戶 VRF。唯一的項目是一個沒有路由的內部項目。
  • P2 有兩個 locator。MAIN 是我們最常用的 locator。第二個 locator 用於 Flex-Algo。第 11 集會說明它。
  • P2 有 12 個本地 SID：它的 node SID 和 adjacency SID。不論有三個客戶還是三千個客戶，P2 保存的狀態都一樣。
1.2 · And what PE1 holds
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show segment-routing srv6 sid
fcbb:bb00:1:e004::          uDT4              'BLUE'                            bgp-65000           InUse  Y
fcbb:bb00:1:e005::          uDT4              'RED'                             bgp-65000           InUse  Y
fcbb:bb00:1:e006::          uDT6              'BLUE'                            bgp-65000           InUse  Y
fcbb:bb00:1:e007::          uDT6              'RED'                             bgp-65000           InUse  Y
fcbb:bb00:1:e00a::          uDT4              'GREEN'                           bgp-65000           InUse  Y

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route vrf all summary
VRF: RED     ...  bgp 65000      2
VRF: BLUE    ...  bgp 65000      2
VRF: GREEN   ...  bgp 65000      1
  • 現在看邊緣。這是同一個完成後實驗裡的 PE1。
  • PE1 為每個客戶的每個位址族各有一個 service SID：BLUE 兩個，RED 兩個，GREEN 一個。
  • PE1 也保存每個客戶來自 BGP 的遠端路由。每個客戶的狀態在邊緣，而且只在邊緣。
1.3 · What the customer sees

router／工具：CE-A

CE-A:~$ sudo traceroute -n -s 10.1.1.2 10.1.6.2 -w 1 -q 1 -m 8
traceroute to 10.1.6.2 (10.1.6.2) from 10.1.1.2, 8 hops max, 46 byte packets
 1  10.1.1.1  1.259 ms
 2  10.1.6.1  2.902 ms
 3  10.1.6.2  1.610 ms
  • 我們從客戶這一側檢查同一件事，從 CE-A 到 CE-B 做一次 traceroute。
  • 第一跳是 PE1，也就是客戶的閘道。
  • 下一跳是 PE6，然後是 CE-B。四台核心路由器沒有出現。它們不碰客戶的封包，只處理外層標頭。

驗收條件： 依每項判讀核對結果。缺少實測結果的項目標為「未驗證」。開始另一個實驗前，還原指定基線。

自測題：

  1. P router 仍保留哪些狀態？
  2. 同一台 router 可以同時具有中繼和 segment endpoint 角色嗎？

接著讀： 第 2 章。先保留本章的正常狀態與觀察紀錄，再進入下一項機制。

02

建立實驗網路並完成驗收

實驗問題：建立可比較的正常狀態

故障只有在與正常狀態比較時才容易定位。本章先固定拓撲、位址和起始設定，再分別驗證 adjacency、local SID 與遠端 locator。每個檢查都回答不同問題；成功 commit 不等於服務已可用。

觀察與判讀： 本章解釋為何要檢查十六個有方向的 adjacency，以及如何確認 PE1 能到達 PE6 locator。

起點狀態： 先完成本章驗收，再進行會改動網路的實驗。若沒有 CML，使用 F03–F05 練習判讀即可，不需假定自己已完成實測。

固定拓撲

核心拓撲：link cost 與服務端點

八條核心 link 共有十六個有方向的 IS-IS adjacency。每台 PE 有兩個鄰居。每台 P router 有三個鄰居。PE1 到 PE6 的最短路徑是 PE1–P2–P4–PE6，成本為 30。

項目 數值
節點 n 的 loopback 2001:db8:100::n/128
MAIN locator fcbb:bb00:n::/48
FA128 locator fcbb:bb01:n::/48
節點 a 與 b 的核心子網路 2001:db8:200:ab::/127
IS-IS 層級 Level 2
BLUE route target 65000:100
RED route target 65000:200

Loopback 位於 locator 以外。因此，可以分別檢查兩者的可達性。區塊和位址規劃都是本實驗的設計選擇。

最小 PE1 範例

以下片段建立 PE1 的核心基線。它不包含管理存取、其他 router、客戶服務或保護功能。interface 名稱必須符合匯入的節點。

interface Loopback0
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:100::1/128
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:200:12::/127
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:200:13::/127
!
segment-routing
 srv6
  encapsulation
   source-address 2001:db8:100::1
  locators
   locator MAIN
    micro-segment behavior unode psp-usd
    prefix fcbb:bb00:1::/48
!
router isis CORE
 is-type level-2-only
 net 49.0001.0000.0000.0001.00
 address-family ipv6 unicast
  metric-style wide
  segment-routing srv6
   locator MAIN
 interface Loopback0
  passive
  address-family ipv6 unicast
 interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
  point-to-point
  address-family ipv6 unicast
   metric 10
 interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1
  point-to-point
  address-family ipv6 unicast
   metric 40

推演案例：先算拓撲，再核對輸出

核心有八條 link。每條 link 的兩端各建立一個有方向的 adjacency，所以全網應記錄十六個。不要把單台 router 顯示的鄰居數，誤當成全網總數。PE1–P2–P4–PE6 的 link 成本總和為 30，這是之後比較路徑的基準。

讀圖順序： F03 用來核對鄰居；F04 用來核對本機 locator 與 SID；F05 用來核對 PE1 的遠端 locator 路由。三張圖分別回答連線、local 安裝與遠端可達性。

先想一想： 如果 F03 正常，但 F05 缺少 PE6 locator，下一步應看哪個節點的通告，而不是重設所有 adjacency？

從證據推理：ping 成功就能驗收 underlay 嗎？

PE1 可以 ping PE6，但 P2 少了一個預期的 adjacency。現在能開始保護機制實驗嗎？

先預測結果，再展開比較判讀

ping 只證明一條路徑可用，不能證明拓撲完整。替代路徑可能掩蓋缺少的 link。

先依拓撲逐一核對鄰居，再檢查 local SID、遠端 locator 路由及 CEF。保護機制需要完整的預期拓撲。

L2 — 驗收基線

起點狀態： 先啟動六台 router，依上圖連接。每條 link 的兩端都要設定。

在指定的 router 或工具執行指令。提示字元與輸出是證據，不要當成指令貼上。

設定區塊須在 configuration mode 輸入。完成一項變更後先 commit，再執行對應檢查。讀取結果後才進行下一項。

傳送測試流量前，先在指定 link 啟動擷取。核對 packet 方向、位址與 header 欄位。

輸出節錄省略無關行。動態 SID 與計數器可不同。只有設定區塊，不代表驗收成功。

階段 · Ep02 — 指令與結果
2.1 · Know what you are running
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show version

Build Information:
 Built By     : cisco
 Built On     : Thu Sep 10 00:39:05 UTC 2026
 Workspace    : /auto/srcarchive13/prod/26.2.2/xrd-vrouter/ws/
 Version      : 26.2.2

cisco XRd vRouter

XRd vRouter Container
  • 在設定任何東西之前，先記錄你使用的軟體。這是每份實驗報告的第一行。
  • 版本是 IOS XR 26.2.2。
  • 平台是 XRd vRouter，一個 container。大部分輸出來自這個平台和版本。XRv9000 比較資料另行標明平台。
2.2 · Step 1: addresses
interface Loopback0
 description router-id and SRv6 encapsulation source
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:100::1/128
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
 description TO-P2 cost 10
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:200:12::/127
 no shutdown
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1
 description TO-P3 cost 40
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:200:13::/127
 no shutdown
  • 設定有三個步驟。這是 PE1。其他五個節點使用同樣的模式。
  • 第一步是位址。Loopback0 使用規劃中的 /128。它是 router ID，也是每個封裝封包的來源位址。
  • 兩個核心介面配上各自的 /127 位址。沒有 IPv4 位址，沒有 MPLS，也沒有 LDP。
2.3 · Step 2: SRv6 and the locator
segment-routing
 srv6
  encapsulation
   source-address 2001:db8:100::1
  !
  locators
   locator MAIN
    micro-segment behavior unode psp-usd
    prefix fcbb:bb00:1::/48
   !
  !
 !
  • 第二步啟用 SRv6。只有四行是重要的。
  • 封裝來源位址是 loopback。當這台路由器封裝客戶封包時，這個位址就是外層的來源位址。
  • Locator 的名稱是 MAIN。它的 prefix 是這個節點的 /48。
  • 這一行讓它成為 micro-SID locator。node SID 是帶有 PSP 和 USD flavor 的 uN。第 4 集會說明這些 flavor。
  • 在硬體平台上，你可能還需要 hardware profile 並重新開機。這台虛擬路由器兩者都不需要。
2.4 · Step 3: IS-IS carries the locator
router isis CORE
 is-type level-2-only
 net 49.0001.0000.0000.0001.00
 address-family ipv6 unicast
  metric-style wide
  segment-routing srv6
   locator MAIN
 !
 interface Loopback0
  passive
  address-family ipv6 unicast
 !
 interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
  point-to-point
  address-family ipv6 unicast
   metric 10
  • 第三步是 IS-IS。這段設定大部分是一般的 IS-IS。
  • 我們啟用 IPv6 address family，並使用 wide metric。
  • 這兩行是 SRv6 的部分。它們把 locator 掛到 IS-IS 上。然後 IS-IS 才會通告 locator，並建立 adjacency SID。
  • 如果少了這兩行，提交仍然成功。Locator 在這台路由器上，但其他路由器都到不了它。
  • 每個核心介面都是點對點，metric 依照我們的規劃。
2.5 · Check 1: IS-IS neighbors

router／工具：P2

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:P2#show isis neighbors

IS-IS CORE neighbors:
System Id      Interface        SNPA           State Holdtime Type IETF-NSF
PE1            Gi0/0/0/0        *PtoP*         Up    28       L2   Capable
P3             Gi0/0/0/2        *PtoP*         Up    23       L2   Capable
P4             Gi0/0/0/1        *PtoP*         Up    28       L2   Capable

Total neighbor count: 3
  • 檢查一，在 P2 上。首先，數一數鄰居，並和拓撲圖比較。
  • P2 有三個鄰居：PE1、P3 和 P4。全部是 up、level 2、點對點。
  • 拓撲圖上也是三個。每台 PE 有兩個鄰居，每台 P 路由器有三個。
2.6 · Check 2: what the router says it can do
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show segment-routing srv6 manager
Parameters:
  SRv6 Enabled: Yes
  SRv6 Operational Mode:
    Micro-segment:
      SID Base Block: fcbb:bb00::/24
  Encapsulation:
    Source Address:
      Default: 2001:db8:100::1
      Configured: 2001:db8:100::1
  SID Formats:
    f3216 <32B/16NFA> (2)
      uSID LIB Range:
        LIB Start   : 0xe000
        ELIB Start  : 0xfe00
      uSID WLIB Range:
        EWLIB Start : 0xfff7
  • 檢查二只有一個指令：show segment-routing srv6 manager。輸出很長，所以我們分三段來讀。
  • SRv6 已啟用，運作模式是 micro-segment。
  • 封裝來源位址就是我們設定的 loopback。
  • SID 格式是 f3216。也就是 32 位元的 block，後面是 16 位元的 node ID 和 function ID。
  • 本地 function 從十六進位 e000 開始。請記住這個數字。這個系列的每一張 SID 表裡都會看到它。
2.7 · Check 2, continued: behaviors
Platform Capabilities:
  SRv6: Yes
  TILFA: Yes
  Microloop-Avoidance: Yes
  Endpoint behaviors:
    uN (PSP/USD)
    uA (PSP/USD)
    uDT6
    uDT4
    uDT46
    uDX2
    uDT2U
    uDT2M
    uB6 (Insert.Red)
  Headend behaviors:
    T
    H.Insert.Red
    H.Encaps.Red
    H.Encaps.L2.Red
  • 第二段列出這台路由器支援的 behavior。
  • uN 和 uA 是節點和鄰接的 behavior。每一條路徑都使用它們。
  • uDT 和 uDX 這幾項是 service behavior。它們用於三層 VPN 和點對點乙太網路。
  • uB6 是 Binding SID。清單裡有某個 behavior，不代表每個相關功能都能用。例如，這個平台拒絕 bridge domain。
  • headend 清單裡有 H.Insert.Red 和 H.Encaps.Red，都是 reduced 形式。它沒有一般的 H.Encaps。
  • 少了這一行，後面每一集的封包都會不同。在設計任何東西之前，先讀這段輸出。
2.8 · Check 2, continued: depth
  Signaled parameters:
    Max-SL          : 3
    Max-End-Pop-SRH : 3
    Max-H-Insert    : 3 sids
    Max-H-Encap     : 3 sids
    Max-End-D       : 4
  Default parameters (under srv6):
    Encapsulation:
      Hop-Limit     : value=0, propagate=No
      Traffic-class : value=0, propagate=No
  Max Locators: 16
  Max SIDs: 64000
  • 第三段是關於限制。
  • 路由器把這些深度通告給鄰居。它可以插入或封裝 3 個 SID。
  • 這裡的 SID 是完整的 128 位元容器。一個容器可以放好幾個 micro-SID。所以 3 這個上限比看起來更大。
  • 預設情況下，路由器不會把客戶封包的 hop limit 和 traffic class 複製到外層標頭。第 13 集會在線路上檢查這一點。
  • 上限是 16 個 locator 和 64000 個 SID。這是虛擬路由器的上限。不要把它們用在硬體上。
2.9 · Check 3: the locator and the local SIDs
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show segment-routing srv6 locator
Name                  ID       Algo  Prefix                    Status   Flags
--------------------  -------  ----  ------------------------  -------  --------
MAIN                  1        0     fcbb:bb00:1::/48          Up       U

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show segment-routing srv6 sid

*** Locator: 'MAIN' ***

SID                         Behavior          Identification                    Owner               State  RW
--------------------------  ----------------  --------------------------------  ------------------  -----  --
fcbb:bb00:1::               uN (PSP/USD)      'default':1                       sidmgr              InUse  Y
fcbb:bb00:1:e000::          uA (PSP/USD)      [Gi0/0/0/0, Link-Local]:0         isis-CORE           InUse  Y
fcbb:bb00:1:e001::          uA (PSP/USD)      [Gi0/0/0/1, Link-Local]:0         isis-CORE           InUse  Y
  • 檢查三使用兩個指令。在這個系列裡，你會比其他任何指令都更常用到它們。
  • locator MAIN 是 up，屬於 algorithm 0，prefix 就是我們設定的那個。
  • 第一個 SID 是 node SID，也就是 uN。它屬於 SID manager。locator 一旦 up，它就存在。
  • 接下來兩個 SID 是 adjacency SID，每個核心介面一個。它們屬於 IS-IS。這就是第三步重要的原因。
  • 它們的 function 是 e000 和 e001。這是本地範圍的頭兩個值。
2.10 · The remote locator, as PE1 sees it
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route ipv6 isis

i L2 2001:db8:100::6/128
      [115/30] via fe80::5454:ff:fe9b:6d1f, 01:12:13, GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
i L2 fcbb:bb00:2::/48
      [115/11] via fe80::5454:ff:fe9b:6d1f, 01:12:32, GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
i L2 fcbb:bb00:4::/48
      [115/21] via fe80::5454:ff:fe9b:6d1f, 01:12:13, GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
i L2 fcbb:bb00:6::/48
      [115/31] via fe80::5454:ff:fe9b:6d1f, 01:12:13, GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0
  • 本地 SID 只有在其他路由器到得了時才有用。所以我們在 PE1 上檢查來自 IS-IS 的路由。
  • PE6 的 loopback metric 是 30，經由 GigabitEthernet 0。這是上方路徑，和我們的預測一樣。
  • PE6 的 locator 是另一條路由，metric 是 31。在這個版本上，路由器會為 locator 在路徑 cost 上加 1。
  • P2 和 P4 的 locator 也在這裡，metric 分別是 11 和 21。每個節點的 locator 都是一條一般的 IPv6 路由。
  • 這是 SRv6 的一個重要特性。中間的路由器不需要新的功能，就能把封包轉送到 SID。它只需要一條路由。
2.11 · Check 4: ping the node SID
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping fcbb:bb00:6:: source 2001:db8:100::1 count 2
Type escape sequence to abort.
Sending 2, 100-byte ICMP Echos to fcbb:bb00:6::, timeout is 2 seconds:
!!
Success rate is 100 percent (2/2), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/3 ms
  • 這是 PE1 上的 ping 指令。目的位址是 PE6 的 node SID，fcbb：bb00：6：：。
  • source 選項設定來源位址。我們使用 PE1 的 loopback，因為每台路由器都到得了它。回覆需要這個位址才能回來。count 選項表示送出兩個封包。
  • 路由器送出兩個 echo request，每個 100 位元組。
  • 每個驚嘆號代表一個收到的回應。
  • 成功率是 100%，2 發 2 中。Ping 成功了。但光是 ping 看不到路徑。為此，我們需要擷取檔。
2.12 · Check 4: the packet on three links

router／工具：tcpdump

# PE1 to P2
IP6 (hlim 60) 2001:db8:100::1 > fcbb:bb00:6::: ICMP6, echo request, seq 0
# P2 to P4
IP6 (hlim 59) 2001:db8:100::1 > fcbb:bb00:6::: ICMP6, echo request, seq 0
# P4 to PE6
IP6 (hlim 58) 2001:db8:100::1 > fcbb:bb00:6::: ICMP6, echo request, seq 0
IP6 (hlim 64) 2001:db8:100::6 > 2001:db8:100::1: ICMP6, echo reply, seq 0
  • 這是 tcpdump 的輸出。每一行是一個封包。每行開頭是 hop limit，接著是來源位址、目的位址和封包類型。我們顯示每個擷取檔中的第一個 echo request。
  • 在第一條鏈路上，目的位址就是這個 SID，hop limit 是 60。
  • 在第二條鏈路上，目的位址相同，hop limit 是 59。
  • 在第三條鏈路上，hop limit 是 58。P2 和 P4 沒有做任何特別的事。它們只是照路由轉送封包。每台路由器把 hop limit 減 1。
  • 最後這一行是第三條鏈路上的回覆。它來自 PE6 的 loopback，2001：db8：100：：6，不是來自那個 SID。

驗收條件： 依每項判讀核對結果。缺少實測結果的項目標為「未驗證」。開始另一個實驗前，還原指定基線。

自測題：

  1. 為何實驗把 loopback 放在 locator 區塊以外？
  2. 為何不能直接使用最終的 PE1 設定執行 VPWS 測試？

接著讀： 第 3 章。先保留本章的正常狀態與觀察紀錄，再進入下一項機制。

03

解讀 SID 並追蹤 packet

實驗問題：把 SID 當成可逐步追蹤的指令

核心拓撲：link cost 與服務端點

前一章確認位址可達。本章進一步區分「依 locator 送往某台 router」與「這台 router 執行 local SID」。接著追蹤 uSID 位移：每次改動的是哪個欄位，下一次查表又使用哪個值。

觀察與判讀： 本章逐跳寫出 destination address，並區分 uN 的節點選擇與 uA 的 adjacency 選擇。

起點狀態： 先使用表中的三節點例子，不要一開始就加入 service SID、跨區塊與修復路徑。

兩種不同的比對

Locator 是可路由的 prefix，用來把 packet 送往某個節點。local SID 項目則告訴該節點應執行哪種行為。

例如，P2 可以使用 fcbb:bb00:6::/48 路由，轉送 destination address 為 fcbb:bb00:6:e004:: 的 packet。P2 不需要 BLUE VRF。packet 到達 PE6 後，更具體的 local service SID 會選擇 BLUE。

解封裝後，PE6 會使用內層 destination address，在 BLUE 再做一次查表。Locator 可達不能取代這次查表。local SID 也不能取代通往客戶的路由。

f3216 與六個位置

fcbb:bb00 : 0006 : e004 : 0000 : 0000 : 0000 : 0000
<32 bits>   <16>   <16>   <16>   <16>   <16>   <16>
  區塊      節點   功能           其餘位置

此格式使用 32-bit 區塊和 16-bit 壓縮識別碼。區塊後方還有六個位置。這些位置可以包含節點指令和 local 功能指令。

六個位置不一定代表六台不同的 router。服務功能會使用一個位置。adjacency 功能也可能使用一個位置。轉換至另一個區塊時，需要另一個 container。

既有 IS-IS 紀錄中的 uN 結構是 32/16/0/80。在該通告中，uN 沒有獨立的功能欄位。其引數可以容納另外五個 16-bit 識別碼。

既有 uA 結構是 32/16/16/64。第 5 章的 BGP 服務屬性則顯示另一種結構。這些通告描述的是不同物件。

行為與附加處理方式

IOS XR 名稱 主要動作 service context
uN 推進至下一個壓縮指令 節點
uA 使用指定 adjacency link
uDT4 解封裝並使用 IPv4 routing table VRF
uDT6 解封裝並使用 IPv6 routing table VRF
uDT46 使用 IPv4 或 IPv6 routing table VRF，須確認支援
uDX2 解封裝並交付 Ethernet frame attachment circuit
uDT2U / uDT2M 使用橋接表或 BUM 交付功能 E-LAN，本實驗未實測
uB6 套用關聯的 policy SR Policy

Cisco 的 uN 和 uA 使用 NEXT-CSID 行為。服務名稱識別對應的端點功能。既有 uB6 實驗使用插入形式。不能只依名稱判斷其封裝動作。

PSP 在倒數第二個 segment endpoint 移除 SRH。USP 在最後一個端點移除 SRH。USD 則在指定條件成立時，於最後一個端點移除外層 IPv6 封裝。

uDT 服務會自行解封裝。此動作不能證明 USD 已執行。實驗實測了 PSP，但沒有完成獨立的 USD 實驗。

三個節點的範例

擷取 link IPv6 destination address Hop Limit
PE1–P2 fcbb:bb00:2:4:6:: 60
P2–P4 fcbb:bb00:4:6:: 59
P4–PE6 fcbb:bb00:6:: 58

在 P2，目前的 uN 識別 P2。P2 把其餘識別碼左移 16 bits，並在最後一個位置補零。P2 再依新的 destination address 轉送。P4 會重複相同的過程。

一般中繼節點會減少 Hop Limit，但不會推進識別碼。因此，Hop Limit 改變不能證明 segment 指令已執行。

完整的端點處理還要檢查剩餘引數、SRH 和 payload。只看到 Segments Left = 0，不能判定所有壓縮指令都已完成。

推演案例：手動追蹤一次 uSID 位移

從 fcbb:bb00:2:4:6:: 開始。P2 執行自己的 uN 後，下一個識別碼成為目前指令，destination address 變成 fcbb:bb00:4:6::。P4 再執行一次，destination address 變成 fcbb:bb00:6::。每次位移後都要依新的位址轉送，並非直接從清單取得實體出口。

讀圖順序： 先讀 F09 的 uN 行為，再用 F11 的 link 與 destination address 欄驗證推論。F12 解釋為何這次 ping 沒有回覆：checksum 問題與沿途位移是否發生，是兩個不同問題。

先想一想： 若只看到 Hop Limit 減少，還缺少哪個欄位的變化，才能證明 uN 已執行？

從證據推理：一個位址是在選路徑，還是選服務？

比較 node 指令與 uDT4 service 指令。兩者都使用 IPv6 位址，接收端的動作卻有何不同？

先預測結果，再展開比較判讀

node 指令推進 transport program；uDT4 移除外層封裝並選擇 IPv4 table。只讀位址，無法判斷實際行為。

先讀 local SID 的 behavior 與 owner，再預測下一次 lookup 使用哪張表、哪些 header 會保留，最後用擷取驗證。

L3 — 觀察位移與 adjacency

起點狀態： 從 GREEN、BLUE 與 MAIN locator 正常的狀態開始。每項故障還原後，再進行下一項。

在指定的 router 或工具執行指令。提示字元與輸出是證據，不要當成指令貼上。

設定區塊須在 configuration mode 輸入。完成一項變更後先 commit，再執行對應檢查。讀取結果後才進行下一項。

傳送測試流量前，先在指定 link 啟動擷取。核對 packet 方向、位址與 header 欄位。

輸出節錄省略無關行。動態 SID 與計數器可不同。只有設定區塊，不代表驗收成功。

3.1 · The egress tables behind it

router／工具：PE6

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show segment-routing srv6 sid fcbb:bb00:6:e006:: detail
fcbb:bb00:6:e006::          uDT4              'RED'                             bgp-65000           InUse  Y
  SID Function: 0xe006
  SID Identification (Context): { table-id=0xe0000001 ('RED':IPv4/Unicast) }

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show cef ipv6 fcbb:bb00:6:e006::/64
fcbb:bb00:6:e006::/64, version 179, SRv6 Endpoint uDT4
    next hop VRF - 'RED', table - 0xe0000001
    0     Y   recursive                 Lookup in table

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE6#show route vrf RED 10.2.6.2
Routing entry for 10.2.6.0/24
  Known via "connected", distance 0, metric 0 (connected)
    directly connected, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/3
  • 這些是完成這項工作的出口 routing table。
  • 這個 SID 是 uDT4。它的 context 是 VRF RED 的 IPv4 routing table。
  • 在 CEF 裡，這個 SID 是一筆一般的 /64 項目。它的動作是在 RED routing table 裡查詢內層 packet。
  • 在 RED 裡，客戶位址直接連接在通往 CE-B 的埠上。這是條件四的證據。
3.2 · Healthy 1: the loopback ping and the locator route
RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#ping 2001:db8:100::6 source 2001:db8:100::1 count 2
Type escape sequence to abort.
Sending 2, 100-byte ICMP Echos to 2001:db8:100::6, timeout is 2 seconds:
!!
Success rate is 100 percent (2/2), round-trip min/avg/max = 2/2/3 ms

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route ipv6 fcbb:bb00:6::/48
Routing entry for fcbb:bb00:6::/48
  Known via "isis CORE", distance 100, metric 31, SRv6-locator, type level-2
  Routing Descriptor Blocks
    fe80::5454:ff:fe66:75e1, from 2001:db8:100::6, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0, Protected
      Route metric is 31
    fe80::5454:ff:fec1:58eb, from 2001:db8:100::6, via GigabitEthernet0/0/0/1, Backup (TI-LFA)
      Repair Node(s): 2001:db8:100::5
      Route metric is 101
  • 我們從健康的實驗環境開始。先做大多數工程師最先做的檢查：ping PE6 的 loopback。
  • destination address 是 2001:db8:100::6，也就是 PE6 的 loopback。source address 是 PE1 的 loopback。
  • 兩個回應都收到了，成功率是 100%。這個 ping 只測試 loopback，並沒有用到 locator。
  • 現在看 locator。PE1 有一條到 fcbb:bb00:6::/48 的路由。IS-IS 安裝了它，路由類型是 SRv6-locator。
  • 主要路徑從 PE1 的 Gi0/0/0/0 送出。路由 metric 是 31。
  • 備援路徑從 Gi0/0/0/1 送出，metric 是 101。請記住：在健康狀態下，PE1 到這個 locator 有一條主要路徑和一條備援路徑。

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show bgp vpnv4 unicast vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32 detail
Paths: (1 available, best #1)
    2001:db8:100::6 (metric 30) from 2001:db8:100::6 (10.0.0.6)
      Received Label 0xe0080
      Origin incomplete, metric 0, localpref 100, valid, internal, best, group-best
      Extended community: RT:65000:300
       SID Locator: fcbb:bb00:6::/48, RIB metric: 31
        T:1(Sid information), Sid:fcbb:bb00:6::(Transposed), Behavior:63
         Length [Loc-blk,Loc-node,Func,Arg]:[32,16,16,0], Tpose-len:16, Tpose-offset:48

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show route vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32
Routing entry for 10.30.6.6/32
  Known via "bgp 65000", distance 200, metric 0, type internal
    2001:db8:100::6, from 2001:db8:100::6
      Nexthop in Vrf: "default", Table: "default", IPv6 Unicast, Table Id: 0xe0800000
  • 接著看客戶路由。在 PE1 上，我們讀 VRF GREEN 裡 10.30.6.6 這個 prefix 的 BGP 詳細輸出。
  • BGP 有一條路徑，來自 PE6。next hop 是 PE6 的 loopback，到它的 IGP metric 是 30。
  • 收到的 label 是 0xe0080。它裡面放著 SID 的 function e008。故障 B 會改變這一行。
  • 這條路徑是 valid 和 best。Route target 65000:300 把這條路由放進 VRF GREEN。
  • BGP 也會檢查 SID 的 locator。這條 locator 路由在 RIB 裡，metric 是 31。故障 A 會改變這一行。
  • 在 VRF 裡，這是一條 BGP 路由。它的 next hop 在 default VRF 的 IPv6 routing table 裡。PE1 必須在那張表裡解析 next hop。

RP/0/RP0/CPU0:PE1#show cef vrf GREEN 10.30.6.6/32
10.30.6.6/32, version 9, SRv6 Headend
   via fcbb:bb00:6::/128, 3 dependencies, recursive

    next hop fcbb:bb00:6::/128 via fcbb:bb00:6::/48
    SRv6 H.Encaps.Red SID-list {fcbb:bb00:6:e008::}

    0     Y   GigabitEthernet0/0/0/0    fe80::5454:ff:fe66:75e1

Sending 3, 100-byte ICMP Echos to 10.30.6.6 timeout is 2 seconds:
!!!
